brief: The evening door has custom from nowhere: `spawnTapAgent` rolls its own arrivals and nothing else in the town sends anybody there. Connect it: when the summer concert strikes (`bandEnd`, the audience's `a.leaveAt`), a share of the audience walks to the door instead of home, so on a concert night the pavement fills within the walk time; on a market day the last stallholder and the sweeper's opposite number call in. While there, fix c65: `scarcity()` reads `agents.length` and the tap crowd is inside it, so a full pavement damps the three night arrival RATES that POP_FLOOR lifts — scarcity must read a population the tap crowd is not part of. And assert c68: `BAND_DUSK` is a hand-computed clearance between the strike ramp and `eastOpen()`; add the check to `probes/bandstand-year.mjs` so moving BAND_DOWN/BAND_LEN/leaveAt fails a probe instead of emptying the green in one frame.
successLooksLike: Folded over ten summer days, the door's occupancy in the hour after bandEnd on concert nights is measurably above ordinary nights, and the walkers who fill it came from BAND_SLOTS (same ids via __entities). scarcity() with four tap agents present equals scarcity() with none. The bandstand probe asserts the clearance.
avoid: Do not add TAP_SLOTS (four; the pavement holds four at 0.9 cells). Price the walk: the bandstand-to-door trip is long — if it exceeds the tap's remaining hours on a winter concert night, send nobody rather than someone who arrives after the shut.
